headline: Geopolitical Fog and Rate Jitters Cloud Friday's Open
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious start this Friday morning as traders absorb a Thursday session that ended fractionally in the red, with the S&P 500 finishing marginally lower amid persistent focus on the US-Iran conflict. Market breadth told a clear story: 326 names in our 545-stock universe declined against only 218 advances, with Materials, Semiconductors, and Industrials bearing the heaviest selling pressure — down 1.2%, 0.96%, and 0.9%, respectively. Healthcare and Homebuilders were the lone bright spots, edging higher by 0.27% and 0.16%.

The macro backdrop heading into the open remains layered. Gold is rising but on pace for a weekly loss as Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations continue to firm, a combination that argues for risk discipline in rate-sensitive names. Oil slid overnight as hopes for a US-Iran truce tempered what might otherwise have been a supply-shock bid, even as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalated and Riyadh's grand mufti called on troops to prepare for sacrifice.

On the data front, watch for any Fed-speak that could sharpen the rate trajectory into month-end. The Iran diplomatic thread — with Tehran's president placing the choice of de-escalation squarely on Washington — will also command attention throughout the session. Volatility in defensives and energy proxies could persist until geopolitical clarity improves.

briefs.headline: Healthcare Diagnostics Stocks Surge to Lead Thursday's Winners
briefs.body: Veracyte and NeoGenomics surged 10.77% and 6.54%, respectively, on Thursday, anchoring a broad rally in diagnostics names. Life-science tools firms Bruker and Revvity added 7.26% and 6.03%, while contract-research outfit Charles River Labs climbed 6.17%. The cluster move suggests renewed institutional appetite for healthcare exposure heading into Friday.

briefs.headline: Acadia Pharma Drops Nearly 13%, Leads Biotech Retreat
briefs.body: Acadia Pharmaceuticals shed 12.78% in Thursday's session, the steepest single-day decline in our universe, dragging on the broader pharma-biotech space. The selloff stood in stark contrast to a separate injectable-drug name that soared 150% on a licensing deal with Novo Nordisk's Wegovy franchise, underscoring the bifurcated nature of biotech risk right now.

briefs.headline: First Solar Slides More Than 10% as Oil Retreat Weighs on Alternatives
briefs.body: First Solar fell 10.32% on Thursday as sliding crude prices — driven by US-Iran truce speculation — reduced the relative urgency of renewable-energy investment narratives. The Solar sector's sensitivity to oil-price signals remains a key watch heading into Friday, particularly if diplomatic headlines around Iran shift tone at the open.

briefs.headline: Arm Holdings Drops Nearly 8%, Deepening Chip-Sector Pressure
briefs.body: Semiconductor IP designer Arm Holdings declined 7.88% on Thursday, amplifying a sector-wide retreat that left Semiconductors down 0.96% in aggregate. The move reinforces the defensive tilt investors are adopting toward chip-linked names amid rising rate expectations and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty that clouds global technology demand.

briefs.headline: Gold Edges Higher but Heads for a Weekly Loss on Rate-Hike Bets
briefs.body: Spot gold is modestly higher in pre-market trade but remains on track to close the week lower as firming Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations bolster the dollar and weigh on non-yielding assets. The tug-of-war between safe-haven demand tied to Middle East tensions and monetary-policy headwinds is likely to keep the metal range-bound into the weekend.

briefs.headline: Nor'easter Watch: Airlines Waive Change Fees as Storm Threatens East Coast
briefs.body: Several major carriers have proactively waived flight-change fees ahead of a nor'easter forecast to affect the Eastern Seaboard, a move that could pressure near-term load-factor metrics for the industry. Investors in travel and consumer-discretionary names should monitor storm-track updates, as significant disruptions could ripple into weekend booking data and early-week guidance commentary.
